sentences.text: Bifidobacterium adolescentis is one of the most frequently encountered bifidobacterial species in the adult human gut microbiota, with a reported prevalence of approximately 60 percent.

A pangenome study of 1,682 genomes identified 203 gene clusters absent from five other human-associated Bifidobacterium species and 2,597 genes predicted to have been acquired by horizontal gene transfer.

The same study reported seven phylogenetic clusters partially associated with strain origin, and co-occurrence with 36 putative beneficial commensals and butyrate-producing taxa in adult gut metagenomes.

Comparative genomics of 543 genomes reported significant differences in genome size and GC content between populations from Asia, Europe and North America, and population-specific carbohydrate-active enzymes.

references.title: Assessment of genome evolution in Bifidobacterium adolescentis indicates genetic adaptation to the human gut.
